featured.title: Who's Paying for the Grid Transition?
featured.subtitle: Australian electricity network costs, source data to dashboard
featured.problem: Australian network charges rose sharply into 2026, but the data explaining why sits across dozens of AER spreadsheets, one per network per year. Nobody can easily see where the money goes or whether the spend is justified.
featured.approach: Built the whole chain: Python ingestion into PostgreSQL, dbt transformations into six tested marts, then a five-page Power BI report version-controlled as TMDL and PBIR. Specified in a full BRD before any of it was built.
points: All 18 regulated networks (13 DNSPs and 5 TNSPs), 2006 to 2024, from AER RIN, determination, DMO/VDO and AEMO sources
The 2024 fleet ran capex 6.5% and opex 1.6% above AER-approved allowances, and the DMO network charge rose 17.7% to $853.34 a year

Found that spend per customer correlates with worse reliability at +0.74, then showed it is customer density driving both (-0.84), not inefficiency. A cost-per-customer league table without a density adjustment measures geography
75 DAX measures on a six-mart star schema, 80 automated dbt tests, and red/amber/green thresholds computed from the data rather than hardcoded
A verification script recomputes all 35 headline figures in SQL and diffs them against what the page renders. 35 of 35 match, after it first caught two real defects
Every known gap in the source data is stated on the page instead of hidden. Only 10 of 18 networks publish a bill breakdown at all

featured.title: Commercial + Fulfilment Analytics
featured.subtitle: Power BI engineering: performance, governance, version control
featured.problem: A reporting layer is only trustworthy if it is fast, access-controlled, and reviewable. This build exists to push those three things rather than the domain.
featured.approach: Databricks medallion pipeline (Bronze to Silver to Gold) feeding a conformed star schema, served through Snowflake into a Power BI report committed entirely as text.
points: 180,519 order lines across 2 fact tables and 9 conformed dimensions, with zero missing foreign keys
60+ DAX measures across 13 display folders, and query response tuned to 164 ms measured in DAX Studio
Market-level row-level security with two roles, plus row-count and foreign-key reconciliation checks
The whole 9-page report is committed as 91,000 lines of TMDL and PBIR text with no binary .pbix, so the semantic model is reviewable as a diff
A cohort retention bug found and fixed along the way, where a blunt filter was wiping row context and reporting retention rates of 499% to 1775%

featured.title: Polimap, geo-analytics platform
featured.subtitle: Master's capstone for a real client, High Distinction
featured.problem: Decision-makers needed Australian electoral and census data as maps and charts they could interrogate, not as raw statistical releases.
featured.approach: Reproducible ETL into PostgreSQL and PostGIS, a FastAPI backend, and a React and Leaflet front end serving maps, charts and tables.
points: Relational schema design and download, clean, standardise, load pipelines producing join-ready tables
Data quality controls for uniqueness, referential integrity and geographic coverage, with zero critical defects in UAT
Runbooks that cut onboarding a new geography from days to hours, plus stakeholder demos and an NDA-compliant handover package
featured.note: Source stays private under the client NDA. Happy to walk through the architecture in a call.
